Within each impact category, the values were normalized according to the maximum among the four cases and are presented on a scale from 0 to 1. 2 GOAL AND SCOPE 2.1 STUDY GOAL The purpose of this study is to determine the CO impact associated with DOE project DE-FE0032254 2 titled, “Bench-Scale Development of Promoted High-Capacity Structured Sorbents.” The system under study is a facility with a nominal CO capture rate of 100,000 TPY at a capacity factor of 85% with a 30- 2 year plant life. The main goal of this life cycle analysis (LCA) is to forecast the metric tons of qualified carbon dioxide that are captured and permanently isolated from the atmosphere using Susteon’s DAC process and sequestration. The U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and Department of Energy (DOE) are the intended audience of this study. 2.2 STUDY SCOPE 2.2.1 Functional Unit of the Study The functional unit of this analysis is one kgCO e captured from the atmosphere and permanently stored in 2 a saline aquifer. As such, quantitative results are normalized to this functional unit. 2.2.2 System Boundary The life cycle stages include raw material extraction, manufacturing and processing, transportation, usage and retail, and waste disposal. Technology Background Susteon’s direct air capture (DAC) technology has two key innovations: (1) a high-capacity CO sorbent 2 resistant to water uptake and thermal and oxidative degradation and (2) a sorbent coated filter geometry capable of high air flow throughput with low pressure drop and direct Joule-heating for efficient CO 2 production/sorbent regeneration.
